title: B62 three-shot vertical slice in the Film Studio product workflow
question: Can the validated Film Studio product admit the exact B62 terminal scene, preserve one frozen non-camera asset/state identity across wide, medium and close, create a fresh reviewable 288-frame three-shot animatic, and retain the historical frame-288 rejection without relaxing its 0.90 threshold?

sharedNonCameraIdentity.rule: All three shots come from the same exact source blend and retain these asset, material, topology, action, contact/core/light and provenance identities; only the timeline-selected camera may vary by shot.

formalSequence: start-1: zero-render product inspection binds manifest, source, shared identity, shot roster and historical rejection
start-2: visible product operator renders exactly frames 1-288 once into fresh evidence and writes per-shot/process/stage receipts
one bounded local ffmpeg process creates the review MP4 from accepted PNG frames
start-3: zero-render reopen verifies persisted typed product state, source unchanged and all outputs exact
start-4: zero-render negative controls plus an auditor independent of the product module re-decode frames/video and recompute all bindings
acceptance: exact current engine parent, exact B62 parents and exact product/tool identities
one clean native arm64 build and no changes outside the three allowed Python paths
one exact source blend and shared non-camera identity across all three shots
exactly 288 fresh finite dynamic 640x360 PNG frames with correct 96/96/96 camera routing
one independently decodable 24 fps three-shot MP4 and a three-keyframe review sheet
historical frame-288 0.93378717684983 > 0.90 rejection retained verbatim while the separate motion-aware correction remains threshold-preserving
all five attacks reject before render, source or completed evidence mutation
independent audit PASS and all resource/counter/config/source invariants PASS
stopRules: Do not create a formal root before source/tool freeze and fresh-root/resource admission pass.
Do not reuse inherited T2 frames as PB.6 product output.
Do not modify the B62 source blend or any retained B62/PB evidence.
Do not remove frame 288, change 0.90, reinterpret 0.93378717684983 as PASS or substitute the later motion-aware result for the retained rejection.
Stop and retain FAIL on wrong camera routing, shared identity drift, duplicate/missing/frozen frames, non-finite pixels, output/resource excess or any unexpected render.
Do not create releases, distribute binaries, sign/notarize, force-push, update other refs, upload LFS, use network during validation or begin PB.7.
claimCeiling: A PASS proves only one inherited stylized B62 scene, one admitted arm64 host, one fresh 640x360 review animatic and the frozen machine/human boundary. It does not prove final-film quality, photorealism, cross-platform behavior, production readiness or autonomous filmmaking.
